title: Adaptive Reasoning for Technical Support
business: Technical support teams handling mixed-complexity customer inquiries.
problem: Support agents waste time manually filtering simple status checks from complex troubleshooting requests, leading to inconsistent response quality and latency.
solution: Deploy Qwen3-4B to dynamically toggle between a high-reasoning 'thinking' mode for complex diagnostics and a low-latency 'non-thinking' mode for routine status updates.
steps: Initialize Qwen3-4B using the Hugging Face transformers library.
Configure the tokenizer's apply_chat_template to default to thinking mode for complex diagnostic prompts.
Implement a soft-switch logic in the application layer to append /no_think to user prompts when the intent classifier identifies a routine query.
Set specific sampling parameters for each mode: Temperature 0.6 for thinking and 0.7 for non-thinking.
Parse the output to strip <think> tags for the final customer-facing response.
outcome: Improved operational efficiency by matching model reasoning depth to the specific complexity of each customer interaction.
limitation: The model may exhibit endless repetitions if greedy decoding is used; check for this by monitoring output logs and ensuring presence_penalty is set to 1.5.

diagram.title: Adaptive Reasoning Workflow
diagram.description: How the system routes user input to the appropriate model mode.

code.content:
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer
# Initialize model
tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('Qwen/Qwen3-4B')
# Apply template with soft switch /no_think for routine queries
messages = [{'role': 'user', 'content': 'What is my order status? /no_think'}]
text = tokenizer.apply_chat_template(messages, tokenize=False, add_generation_prompt=True, enable_thinking=True)
# Generate response without thinking block due to soft switch
code.explanation: This snippet demonstrates using the soft switch /no_think to override the default thinking mode for a routine query, mapping directly to the Adaptive Reasoning for Technical Support scenario.
